prompt: Answers keep stopping mid-sentence even though the model clearly had more to say.
why: The response hit its max-token limit; raise it.
trap: A content filter would block, not cut cleanly at a length.

prompt: Finance wants every reply capped so no single answer can run up a large bill.
why: Max tokens bounds output length, and output tokens are billed.
trap: A smaller model is cheaper per token but doesn't cap length.

prompt: Replies are sent by text message and must stay short.
why: A low max-token limit enforces brevity.
trap: The system prompt can ask for brevity, but max tokens guarantees a ceiling.

prompt: A 600-word answer is cut off although the limit was set to 600. A colleague assumed the limit counted words.
why: The limit counts tokens, and English averages about 3/4 of a word per token, so 600 tokens is roughly 450 words.
trap: The limit is fine as a concept; the unit is tokens.
